title: Freedom House Ambulance Service: American Sirens

sentences.en: When people ask me what my favorite episode of 99% Invisible is, I have a hard time answering.
sentences.zh: 每当有人问我《99% Invisible》里我最喜欢哪一集时，我都很难回答。

sentences.en: Not because they're all my precious little babies or some such nonsense, but mostly because
sentences.zh: 这倒不是因为它们都是我的心头肉之类的废话，主要是因为

sentences.en: I just can't remember them all, and there's no simple criteria to judge them against each
sentences.zh: 我根本记不住所有集数，而且也没有什么简单的标准能把它们放在一起

sentences.en: But the show I want to play for you today is definitely in contention for the best episode
sentences.zh: 但我今天要放给你们听的这一集，绝对有资格角逐我们制作过的

sentences.en: It just has everything, engaging storytellers, brilliant reporting, and a compelling history
sentences.zh: 它应有尽有：引人入胜的讲述者、精彩绝伦的报道，以及一段令人震撼的历史，

sentences.en: of a moment when the world really changed.
sentences.zh: 记录了一个世界真正发生改变的时刻。

sentences.en: It's called the Freedom House Ambulance Service.
sentences.zh: 它叫《自由之屋救护车服务》（Freedom House Ambulance Service）。

sentences.en: It originally aired in the summer of 2020, when a lot of the fundamental aspects of work,
sentences.zh: 它最初于2020年夏天播出，当时许多关于工作、

sentences.en: life, health, law enforcement, structural racism, cities, they were all being questioned by
sentences.zh: 生活、健康、执法、结构性种族主义、城市等方面的基本问题，都在被

sentences.en: more and more people because of COVID and the George Floyd protests.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人质疑，原因就是新冠疫情和乔治·弗洛伊德抗议活动。

sentences.en: Kevin Hazard, who reported this piece, subsequently released a whole book on Freedom House called
sentences.zh: 负责报道这篇专题的凯文·哈扎德（Kevin Hazard）随后出版了一本关于“自由之屋”的完整著作，书名是

sentences.en: American Sirens, The Incredible Story of the Black Men Who Became America's First Paramedic.
sentences.zh: 《美国警笛：成为美国首批急救医生的黑人们的不可思议的故事》（American Sirens, The Incredible Story of the Black Men Who Became America's First Paramedic）。

sentences.en: It should be on all your Christmas lists.
sentences.zh: 它应该出现在你们所有人的圣诞礼物清单上。

sentences.en: To celebrate the book's release, I'm proud to represent to you the remarkable story of the
sentences.zh: 为了庆祝这本书的发布，我很荣幸向大家介绍这段非凡的
“自由之屋”救护车服务的故事。

sentences.en: Back in the 1960s and 70s in the city of Pittsburgh, there was a nickname for guys like John Moon,
sentences.zh: 回到20世纪60和70年代的匹兹堡市，像约翰·穆恩（John Moon）这样的人有一个绰号，

sentences.en: Which simply meant that no matter where you went for a job, nobody would hire you.
sentences.zh: 意思很简单，无论你去哪里找工作，都没人会雇佣你。

sentences.en: Moon grew up in Pittsburgh's largely black and economically depressed Hill District.
sentences.zh: 穆恩在匹兹堡以黑人为主且经济萧条的希尔区（Hill District）长大。

sentences.en: In better times, the Hill had its own Negro League baseball team and jazz clubs that hosted
sentences.zh: 在更好的年代，希尔区曾拥有自己的黑人联盟棒球队，还有接待过
艾灵顿公爵（Duke Ellington）和路易斯·阿姆斯特朗（Louis Armstrong）的爵士俱乐部。

sentences.en: But by the time Moon was graduating high school in the late 1960s, there was no escaping the
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪60年代末穆恩高中毕业时，他已经无法逃脱
社区那种“不可雇佣”的污名了。

sentences.en: The reputation was there that I don't want to go to the Hill because you may get beat up.
sentences.zh: 当时的名声是：我不想去希尔区，因为你可能会被打。

sentences.en: You have drug addicts and alcoholics.
And that same label was placed on myself and I understood that.
sentences.zh: 同样的标签也贴在了我身上，我对此心知肚明。

sentences.en: But just because that was your thought doesn't necessarily mean that I had to live up to it.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅因为你们那么想，并不代表我就必须活成那个样子。

sentences.en: So Moon was glad to land a well-paying job right out of school at the local steel mill,
sentences.zh: 所以穆恩很高兴一毕业就在当地钢铁厂找到了一份高薪工作，

sentences.en: only to discover that the hours weren't as reliable as he had hoped.
sentences.zh: 结果却发现工作时间并不像他希望的那样稳定。

sentences.en: Next, he was an orderly at Pittsburgh's Presbyterian University Hospital,
sentences.zh: 接下来，他在匹兹堡长老会大学医院（Presbyterian University Hospital）当护工，

sentences.en: which provided steady employment, but not much else.
sentences.zh: 这份工作虽然稳定，但也就仅此而已了。

sentences.en: All I was doing was making beds and taking people back and forth to the operating room
sentences.zh: 我每天做的就是铺床、把病人推来推去送进手术室，

sentences.en: and lifting and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 还有搬运东西之类的杂活。

sentences.en: Mechanical things where you didn't have to think.
sentences.zh: 都是些不需要动脑子的机械性工作。

sentences.en: For a while, Moon tried his best to find meaning in the work.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，穆恩尽力想从工作中找到意义。

sentences.en: But there was a part of me that said, there has to be something more that I can do.
sentences.zh: 但我内心深处有个声音在说，我一定能做些更有意义的事。

sentences.en: Then one night, halfway through the graveyard shift, Moon watched as two men burst through
sentences.zh: 一天深夜，在值完一半夜班时，穆恩看到两个人冲进了

sentences.en: They were working desperately to save a dying patient.
sentences.zh: 他们正在拼命抢救一名垂死的病人。

sentences.en: And as they rushed by, Moon stood pressed against the wall and wondered,
sentences.zh: 当他们匆匆跑过时，穆恩紧贴着墙站着，心想：

sentences.en: How did they get to be able to do that?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么学会这些本领的？

sentences.en: Maybe today, he wouldn't bat an eye at this scene.
sentences.zh: 也许换做今天，他会对这一幕视而不见。

sentences.en: But in 1970, nothing about it made sense.
sentences.zh: 但在1970年，这一切都让人费解。

sentences.en: The two men weren't doctors, and they weren't nurses.
sentences.zh: 那两个人不是医生，也不是护士。

sentences.en: And their strange white uniforms weren't hospital issue.
sentences.zh: 他们那身奇怪的白色制服也不是医院发的。

sentences.en: But these guys came in with a certain type of confidence.
sentences.zh: 但这些人进来时带着一种特别的自信。

sentences.en: That was just shocking to me from the very point that they came into the room.
sentences.zh: 从他们走进房间的那一刻起，就让我感到无比震惊。

sentences.en: And they had an emblem on their breasts.
sentences.zh: 他们的胸前有一个徽章。
那瞬间勾起了我的兴趣。

sentences.en: The emblem was the two-snaked caduceus, the traditional sign of medicine and healing.
sentences.zh: 那个徽章是双蛇杖，是医学和治愈的传统标志。

sentences.en: But just below the familiar symbol was a word John Moon had never seen before.
sentences.zh: 但在那个熟悉的标志下方，有一个约翰·穆恩从未见过的词。

sentences.en: Moon wasn't familiar with the term paramedic.
sentences.zh: 穆恩对“急救医生”这个词并不熟悉。

sentences.en: Because back then, no one was.
sentences.zh: 因为在当时，没人熟悉这个词。
说话的是记者凯文·哈扎德。

sentences.en: Moon was witnessing the birth of a new profession.
sentences.zh: 穆恩当时见证了一个新职业的诞生。

sentences.en: One that would go on to change the face of emergency medicine.
sentences.zh: 一个后来改变了急救医学面貌的职业。

sentences.en: But to Moon, perhaps the most striking thing of all was that these first-ever paramedics looked like him.
sentences.zh: 但对穆恩来说，最让他震撼的或许是这些首批急救医生看起来和他一样。

sentences.en: I'm standing here looking at these two guys, and I'm saying to myself,
sentences.zh: 我站在那儿看着这两个人，心里对自己说：

sentences.en: my God, these are black guys.
Never before had Moon seen young African-American men performing that kind of work.
sentences.zh: 穆恩从未见过年轻的非裔美国人在从事那种工作。

sentences.en: These were two guys that had afros and beards.
sentences.zh: 这两个人留着爆炸头，蓄着胡子。

sentences.en: And the staff on the floor gave them a level of respect that amazed me.
sentences.zh: 而且楼里的医护人员对他们表现出的尊重程度让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And there's something I never really mentioned to anyone.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事我从未真正向任何人提起过。

sentences.en: I actually snuck off of the floor, and I actually followed them out to the vehicle.
sentences.zh: 我其实偷偷溜出了病房，跟着他们走到了车边。

sentences.en: Because I wanted to see what prompted them to show such proudness and boldness.
sentences.zh: 因为我想看看是什么让他们表现得如此自豪和大胆。

sentences.en: Once I looked at that vehicle, pull off, it was almost like, there goes my job.
sentences.zh: 当我看着那辆车开走时，感觉就像是：我的工作在那儿，

sentences.en: That's what I want to do.
Moon vowed right then, halfway through his long night shift, to become a paramedic.
sentences.zh: 穆恩就在那个漫长夜班的中途发誓，一定要成为一名急救医生。

sentences.en: And in Pittsburgh, in 1970, the only place to do that was an organization called Freedom House Ambulance Service.
sentences.zh: 而在1970年的匹兹堡，唯一能实现这个目标的地方是一个叫“自由之屋救护车服务”的组织。

sentences.en: So I went and applied to get a job with them.
sentences.zh: 所以我去申请了他们的工作。

sentences.en: But that history about how a group of young black men from Pittsburgh became the world's first paramedics is still largely unknown.
sentences.zh: 但关于这群来自匹兹堡的年轻黑人是如何成为世界上第一批急救医生的历史，至今仍鲜为人知。
我自己也曾是一名急救医生。

sentences.en: I did this job for 10 years.
And you'd think the profession's origin story would be a big deal.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得这个职业的起源故事应该很有名。

sentences.en: But the truth is, most of the EMTs I've talked to have never heard of the Freedom House paramedics.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我交谈过的大多数急救人员（EMT）从未听说过“自由之屋”的急救医生。

sentences.en: Or understand what we owe them.
sentences.zh: 也不了解我们欠他们多少。

sentences.en: Today, it's easy to take what paramedics do for granted.
sentences.zh: 今天，人们很容易把急救医生的工作视为理所当然。

sentences.en: Call 911 and they'll arrive with cardiac monitors, airway equipment, and an array of pharmaceuticals to treat anything from heart attacks to gunshots to premature births.
sentences.zh: 拨打911，他们就会带着心脏监护仪、气道设备和各种药物赶到，治疗从心脏病发作、枪伤到早产等各种病症。

sentences.en: But for a long time, emergency medical service, or what today is called EMS, didn't provide anything resembling that.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，紧急医疗服务（即今天的EMS）并不提供任何类似的服务。

sentences.en: In the early days of what we would view as EMS, it really wasn't the equivalent of what we see today.
sentences.zh: 在我们所认为的EMS早期，它确实不是我们今天看到的那样。

sentences.en: They would do whatever it was they knew to do.
sentences.zh: 他们只会做他们知道该做的事。

sentences.en: But, you know, were they doing the right thing?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他们做的是对的吗？
说话的是理查德·克林奇（Richard Clinchy）。

sentences.en: He's the president of the EMS Museum and a trained paramedic.
sentences.zh: 他是EMS博物馆的馆长，也是一名受过培训的急救医生。

sentences.en: Clinchy says that when he started an emergency care in the late 50s, emergency services didn't provide treatment at the scene, or even necessarily on the way to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 克林奇说，当他在50年代末开始从事急救护理时，急救服务并不在现场提供治疗，甚至在去医院的路上也不一定提供。

sentences.en: They were just about getting you to the hospital as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们的任务只是尽快把你送到医院。

sentences.en: Which kind of makes sense in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，这确实有道理。

sentences.en: It is, after all, where the doctors are.
But as a result, it often wasn't clear whose responsibility it was to rush to the scene of an accident.
sentences.zh: 但结果就是，往往不清楚到底该由谁负责赶往事故现场。

sentences.en: Before the evolution of EMS, who did you call?
Well, I was a paid firefighter back in the 60s, and sometimes we got the call.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在60年代是一名带薪消防员，有时我们会接到电话。

sentences.en: If somebody needed a fire truck in the seat of New York, there were fireboxes everywhere.
sentences.zh: 如果有人在纽约需要消防车，到处都有火警报警箱。

sentences.en: You'd pull the handle, and fire personnel and fire equipment would show up.
sentences.zh: 你拉动把手，消防人员和设备就会出现。

sentences.en: In other areas, the responsibility for transporting patients often fell to local funeral homes.
sentences.zh: 在其他地区，运送病人的责任通常落在当地的殡仪馆身上。

sentences.en: You're having a massive heart attack, your life's in the balance, and who rolls up to save you?
sentences.zh: 你突发严重心脏病，生命垂危，谁来救你？
两个开着灵车的殡葬承办人。

sentences.en: But in many major cities, this crucial task fell to another municipal service that probably had even less business responding to medical emergencies.
sentences.zh: 但在许多大城市，这项关键任务落在了另一个市政部门身上，而他们可能更不适合应对医疗紧急情况。

sentences.en: In the area where I was a firefighter, we had a police department that had a 57 Chevrolet wagon.
sentences.zh: 在我当消防员的地区，我们的警察局有一辆57年的雪佛兰旅行车。

sentences.en: That was an emergency response vehicle.
So the idea the general public was faced with was more or less what I would call swoop and scoop, which simply meant that you'd call the police,
sentences.zh: 所以公众面对的理念，多多少少就是我所说的“冲过去，铲起来”，意思很简单：你打给警察，

sentences.en: they'd rush the person out there to you, and then they'd pick you up, put you in the back, and rush you back down to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他们冲到你那儿，把你抬起来，扔进后座，然后飞速把你送回医院。

sentences.en: With minimal training and equipment, John Moon says police departments could do little more than offer patients basic first aid, a canvas stretcher, a half-empty oxygen tank,
sentences.zh: 约翰·穆恩说，由于缺乏培训和设备，警察局除了提供基本的急救、帆布担架、半空的氧气瓶
和一个枕头外，几乎做不了什么。

sentences.en: Which more often than not, only served to choke off the patient's airway.
sentences.zh: 而这些东西往往只会堵塞病人的气道。

sentences.en: And on top of that, both individuals, meaning police officers, got up front and left you back there by yourself.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是，两名警察都坐在前排，把你一个人留在后座。

sentences.en: So if you stopped breathing by the time you arrived, you were perhaps DOA because no one had done anything for you.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在到达医院前停止了呼吸，你可能就直接被宣告死亡了，因为没人为你做任何处理。

sentences.en: The police simply didn't have the tools, the training, or the disposition to save people in a medical emergency.
sentences.zh: 警察根本没有工具、培训或意愿去挽救医疗紧急情况下的病人。

sentences.en: But in the absence of a dedicated emergency medical service, the job was being left to them by default.
sentences.zh: 但在缺乏专门的紧急医疗服务的情况下，这项工作默认就落在了他们头上。

sentences.en: And perhaps nowhere was the problem of relying on the police for help more vividly illustrated than in Pittsburgh's largely black Hill district.
sentences.zh: 而在匹兹堡以黑人为主的希尔区，这种依赖警察救助的问题表现得最为明显。

sentences.en: Moon says the city's mostly white police force was often slow to respond to emergencies in the Hill, while the black residents, for their part,
sentences.zh: 穆恩说，该市以白人为主的警察部队在希尔区应对紧急情况时往往反应迟缓，而黑人居民方面，

sentences.en: were reluctant to even call the police to begin with.
sentences.zh: 一开始甚至不愿意打给警察。

sentences.en: Because there was a trust issue with the police, primarily because there were no constraints.
sentences.zh: 因为存在信任问题，主要是因为警察没有任何约束。

sentences.en: I mean, they could do whatever they wanted, and there was no repercussion or consequences for their actions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们可以为所欲为，而且他们的行为不会受到任何惩罚或后果。

sentences.en: No one wanted to get into the exact same police van that the cops had threatened to throw them in the day before.
sentences.zh: 没人想坐进前一天警察威胁要扔他们进去的那种警车里。

sentences.en: So there was issues all the way around.
Do I really want to call the police?
Chances are they're going to take their time getting here, number one.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们很可能磨磨蹭蹭才到。

sentences.en: And if I wait too long, then chances are a cab won't come to my neighborhood, primarily because of fear of being robbed, or whatever the case is.
sentences.zh: 如果我等太久，出租车也不会来我们社区，主要是因为怕被抢劫，或者诸如此类的情况。

sentences.en: So the options were very limited during that time.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的选择非常有限。

sentences.en: And the same was true to varying degrees in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 全国其他地区在不同程度上也是如此。

sentences.en: Whether a neighborhood was served by the police, or the fire department, or the local funeral home,
sentences.zh: 无论一个社区是由警察、消防队还是当地殡仪馆提供服务，

sentences.en: so long as the priority was transportation as opposed to treatment, no one even realized that there was a job that needed doing.
sentences.zh: 只要优先考虑的是“运送”而不是“治疗”，就没人意识到还有一项工作需要完成。

sentences.en: But then, in the mid-60s, something happened which flipped the paradigm for emergency care on its head,
sentences.zh: 但后来，在60年代中期，发生了一件事，彻底颠覆了急救护理的范式，

sentences.en: and laid the groundwork for the invention of paramedicine.
sentences.zh: 并为急救医学的发明奠定了基础。

sentences.en: In 1966, the federal government published a white paper that would prove so influential
sentences.zh: 1966年，联邦政府发布了一份白皮书，其影响力之大，

sentences.en: that even now, in EMS circles, it is simply called the white paper.
sentences.zh: 以至于即使在今天，在EMS圈子里，它也被简称为“白皮书”。

sentences.en: Basically, it told us we were killing over 50,000 people a year on the highways,
sentences.zh: 基本上，它告诉我们，我们每年在公路上有超过5万人死亡，

sentences.en: and doing so unnecessarily, that there was a way to intervene and save those people.
sentences.zh: 而且这种死亡是不必要的，是有办法干预并挽救这些人的。

sentences.en: But we didn't have the people, nor the resources, nor the training, to do a whole lot about it.
sentences.zh: 但我们当时既没有人员，也没有资源，更没有培训来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Techniques practiced by combat medics overseas had been largely ignored by the medical community,
sentences.zh: 海外战地医护人员实践的技术在很大程度上被医学界忽视了，

sentences.en: with the result that a person was more likely to die of a gunshot wound in America than on a battlefield in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，一个人在美国死于枪伤的可能性比在越南战场上还要大。

sentences.en: The white paper shamed the government into providing money for EMS development on the local level,
sentences.zh: 这份白皮书让政府感到羞愧，从而为地方层面的EMS发展提供了资金。

sentences.en: and government officials and local community leaders began searching for solutions,
sentences.zh: 政府官员和当地社区领袖开始寻求解决方案，

sentences.en: including a community organizer in Pittsburgh named Phil Hallen.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一位名叫菲尔·哈伦的匹兹堡社区组织者。

sentences.en: Oh my God, why do I do this?
sentences.zh: 天哪，我为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Hallen is a former ambulance attendant who came to Pittsburgh in the early 60s.
sentences.zh: 哈伦曾是一名救护车随车人员，于60年代初来到匹兹堡。

sentences.en: And yes, he hates being interviewed.
Okay, how long are we going to be going on this?
I don't last very long at age 90.
Hallen ran a civil rights organization called the Maurice Falk Medical Fund,
sentences.zh: 哈伦曾经营一个名为莫里斯·福克医学基金的民权组织，

sentences.en: which examined health disparities due to institutional racism,
sentences.zh: 该组织专门研究因制度性种族主义导致的健康差距，

sentences.en: and he immediately focused his ire on the city's pitiful emergency services.
sentences.zh: 他立刻将矛头对准了该市糟糕的紧急服务系统。

sentences.en: What was your impression of the level of care that was available in Pittsburgh?
sentences.zh: 你对当时匹兹堡提供的医疗水平有什么印象？

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't my impression of it.
It was the way it was, you know.
sentences.zh: 那就是当时的情况，你懂的。

sentences.en: There wasn't any level of care.
sentences.zh: 根本谈不上什么医疗水平。

sentences.en: There was no such thing as emergency medicine or any of the things we now look back on it
sentences.zh: 当时根本没有急救医学这回事，也没有任何我们现在回过头来看，

sentences.en: and think, well, what the hell was going on?
sentences.zh: 会觉得“天哪，当时到底在搞什么？”的东西。

sentences.en: He could see that what was going on was effectively a public health crisis
sentences.zh: 他看得出来，当时的情况实际上是一场公共卫生危机，

sentences.en: that was disproportionately affecting black neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 而且对黑人社区的影响尤为严重。

sentences.en: But then one day, Hallen came across an article in the local paper
sentences.zh: 但有一天，哈伦在当地报纸上看到了一篇文章，

sentences.en: about a black-operated jobs training program based in the Hill District called Freedom House.
sentences.zh: 是关于希尔区一个由黑人运营的职业培训项目，名叫“自由之家”。

sentences.en: The article described how Freedom House had rolled out a kind of mobile grocery store
sentences.zh: 文章描述了“自由之家”如何推出了一种移动杂货店，

sentences.en: for black neighborhoods, using trucks to bring fresh vegetables to people's doors.
sentences.zh: 用卡车把新鲜蔬菜送到黑人社区居民的家门口。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, health care is terrible in the Hill District.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，希尔区的医疗条件太糟糕了。

sentences.en: If they could run a grocery van around, why can't we run a medical van around or something like that?
sentences.zh: 如果他们能开着杂货车到处跑，为什么我们不能开着医疗车到处跑呢？

sentences.en: Hallen wasn't envisioning anything like modern emergency medical services.
sentences.zh: 哈伦当时设想的并不是现代意义上的急救医疗服务。

sentences.en: At first, he just thought Freedom House's trucks could help transport people
sentences.zh: 起初，他只是认为“自由之家”的卡车可以帮忙运送，

sentences.en: in underserved neighborhoods to the hospital
sentences.zh: 把医疗资源匮乏社区的人送到医院，

sentences.en: and that they could hire people from the Hill District to drive them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可以雇佣希尔区的人来开车。

sentences.en: But that's when I got the director of the university hospital on this group as well.
sentences.zh: 但就在那时，我把大学医院的院长也拉进了这个小组。

sentences.en: And, you know, before the first meeting was over, he said,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，第一次会议还没结束，他就说，

sentences.en: Oh, my God, we have to go immediately to Saffer.
sentences.zh: “天哪，我们必须立刻去找萨弗。”

sentences.en: The experimental study you are about to see is one of 18 similar studies
sentences.zh: 你即将看到的实验研究是18项类似研究之一，

sentences.en: during which we compared various methods of artificial respiration.
sentences.zh: 在这些研究中，我们比较了各种人工呼吸方法。

sentences.en: Dr. Peter Saffer was the head of anesthesiology at the University of Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 彼得·萨弗医生是匹兹堡大学麻醉学系主任。

sentences.en: And by that time, he was already famous in medical circles.
sentences.zh: 那时，他在医学界已经很有名了。

sentences.en: Saffer was a pure scientist and a very precise and impatient Austrian.
sentences.zh: 萨弗是一位纯粹的科学家，也是一位非常严谨且缺乏耐心的奥地利人。

sentences.en: We simulated field conditions by selecting as subjects men and women of various body types.
sentences.zh: 我们通过选择各种体型的男女作为受试者，模拟了现场条件。

sentences.en: This is a film of Saffer from 1951,
sentences.zh: 这是一段1951年拍摄的萨弗的影片，

sentences.en: demonstrating a new technique he developed for resuscitation,
sentences.zh: 展示了他开发的一种新的复苏技术，
也就是我们今天所说的心肺复苏术（CPR）。

sentences.en: To help orient you, we have made a diagram of the experimental setup.
sentences.zh: 为了让你了解情况，我们制作了实验装置的示意图。

sentences.en: Saffer understood that, to be effective,
resuscitation needed to be started immediately by the first person on the scene.
sentences.zh: 复苏必须由现场的第一目击者立即开始。

sentences.en: But he faced heavy resistance from the medical community,
sentences.zh: 但他遭到了医学界的强烈抵制，

sentences.en: which felt the general public couldn't be trusted with such specialized knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们认为普通大众无法掌握这种专业知识。
于是萨弗进行了一项实验。

sentences.en: By anesthetizing and curarizing these subjects, we simulated limp asphyxia victiMs.
sentences.zh: 通过对这些受试者进行麻醉和肌松处理，我们模拟了窒息昏迷的受害者。

sentences.en: Saffer paralyzed a group of volunteers using a chemical compound from the Amazon,
sentences.zh: 萨弗用一种来自亚马逊的化合物麻痹了一群志愿者，
这种化合物通常用于涂毒箭。

sentences.en: Let's just say medical testing has changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 只能说，医学测试已经发生了巨大的变化。

sentences.en: Once the volunteers could no longer breathe on their own,
sentences.zh: 一旦志愿者无法再自主呼吸，

sentences.en: Saffer had untrained laypeople use CPR to keep those volunteers alive.
sentences.zh: 萨弗就让未经训练的普通人用CPR来维持这些志愿者的生命。

sentences.en: And when I say untrained laypeople, I mean children.
sentences.zh: 当我提到未经训练的普通人时，我是指孩子们。

sentences.en: This boy scout will perform mouth-to-airway breathing.
sentences.zh: 这位童子军将演示口对气道呼吸法。

sentences.en: Ultimately, Saffer's views would be vindicated.
sentences.zh: 最终，萨弗的观点得到了证实。

sentences.en: And for his effort, he'd forever be known as the father of CPR.
sentences.zh: 而他的努力，让他永远被称为“心肺复苏之父”。

sentences.en: Hallin already knew some of this when he walked into Peter Saffer's office in 1966.
sentences.zh: 1966年哈伦走进彼得·萨弗的办公室时，已经了解了一些情况。

sentences.en: But nothing could have prepared him for what actually happened.
sentences.zh: 但没有什么能让他为接下来发生的事情做好准备。

sentences.en: Within seconds of greeting Hallin and the Freedom House team,
sentences.zh: 在问候哈伦和“自由之家”团队后的几秒钟内，

sentences.en: the wiry and energetic Saffer began to unleash a torrent of ideas.
sentences.zh: 精干而充满活力的萨弗就开始滔滔不绝地提出各种想法。

sentences.en: Basically, he said, you are just what I'm looking for.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他说，你们正是我要找的人。

sentences.en: I've been trying to figure out how to take rescue breathing and the rest out on the street
sentences.zh: 我一直在想如何把人工呼吸和其他急救技术带到街头，

sentences.en: and to train people how to do that.

sentences.zh: 但萨弗并没有就此止步。

sentences.en: He wasn't content to just teach some van drivers CPR.
sentences.zh: 他不满足于只教几个货车司机做CPR。

sentences.en: I said, let's go beyond that.
Let's train them to be professionals as well.
sentences.zh: 让我们把他们也培养成专业人员。

sentences.en: Professionals who could provide high-quality medical care
sentences.zh: 这些专业人员可以在病人被送往医院之前，

sentences.en: before the person was even taken to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 就提供高质量的医疗护理。

sentences.en: It was not go to the scene, pick up a patient,
sentences.zh: 那不是简单的赶到现场、接上病人、

sentences.en: transport to a hospital, and then start care.
sentences.zh: 运往医院，然后再开始治疗。

sentences.en: It was emergency treatment right there on the pavement.
sentences.zh: 而是在路面上就进行紧急治疗。
萨弗主张，救护车不应只是改装的货运空间，

sentences.en: Saffer argued that ambulances should be mobile intensive care units
sentences.zh: 而应该是移动的重症监护室，

sentences.en: staffed by professionals trained to use cardiac monitors,
sentences.zh: 配备受过专业训练的人员，能够使用心脏监护仪、

sentences.zh: 施用药物，以及采取任何其他可能挽救病人生命的措施。

sentences.en: Hallin and the others could barely keep up.
sentences.zh: 哈伦和其他人都快跟不上他的节奏了。

sentences.en: Saffer wasn't proposing a simple update to the existing system,
sentences.zh: 萨弗提出的不仅仅是对现有系统的简单更新，

sentences.en: but to change the whole culture of pre-hospital care.
sentences.zh: 而是要改变整个院前护理的文化。

sentences.en: And he wanted to do it using Freedom House.
sentences.zh: 而且他想通过“自由之家”来实现这一点。
